sentences.text:
Lanceton D Souza vs The State Of Karanataka on 6 October,
2025
Author: Dipankar Datta

Bench: Dipankar Datta
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2025
 [@ Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 618 Of 2025]
 Lanceton D Souza Appellant
 Versus
 The State Of Karanataka Respondent
 Order
1. Leave granted.
2
The appellant was driving a jeep on 6 th November, 2011.
The jeep was moving behind a mini bus.
While overtaking the said mini bus, the jeep dashed against Sanjeeva Shetty (the deceased) who was walking by the side of the road.
As a result, Sanjeeva Shetty fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He succumbed on the way to Wenlock hospital.
Yathish, another pedestrian, who was a minor on the date of the accident was also hit.
Having suffered a fracture on his leg, Yathish survived.
3. There are concurrent findings of the trial and appellate courts convicting the appellant under Sections 304A, 338 and 279, Indian Penal Code, 1860 1.
The appellant had been sentenced to six months simple imprisonment together with fine of Rs.2,000/- (Rupees two thousand) only by the trial court.

The High Court by the impugned revisional judgment and order dated 26 th November,
2024 set aside the conviction under Section 279, IPC but maintained the conviction under the other sections.
The sentence, however, was affirmed by the appellate court and the High Court.
1 IPC 4. Notice was issued on 14th February, 2025, limited to the question of sentence.
5. We have heard S. N. Bhat, learned senior counsel for the appellant and D. L. Chidananda, learned counsel for the State of Karnataka-respondent.

sentences.text:
It appears from the documents placed on record that the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Mangalore2 was approached by the family members of the deceased victim as well as the injured victim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, separately.

Upon considering the materials on record, by a common award dated 6th December, 2013, the MACT disposed of the two claims by awarding a sum of Rs.5,60,000/- (Rupees five lakh and sixty thousand) only to the family members of the deceased victim and Rs.1,10,850/- (Rupees one lakh ten thousand eight hundred fifty) only to the injured victim, together with current and future interest @ 6% p.a. as just and fair compensation.

7. We are of the considered opinion that interest of justice would be best served if the term imprisonment is set aside, and the sentence for a period of six months imposed on the appellant is altered to an increased amount of fine of Rs. 7,00,000/- (Rupees seven lakh) only to be paid by the appellant.
Ordered accordingly.

8. Within a period of three months from date, the appellant shall deposit a sum of Rs. 7,00,000/-
(Rupees seven lakh) only with the MACT.

Out of such sum, the MACT shall disburse Rs.5,85,000/-
(Rupees five lakh eighty five thousand) only to the heirs of the deceased victim, who were the claimants before it.
The balance amount of Rs.1,15,000/- (Rupees one lakh fifteen thousand) shall be paid to the injured victim.

For such purpose, the MACT shall issue notice to the claimants and the injured victim and upon recording satisfaction as to the 2 MACT identity of the noticees, proceed to comply with this order.
9.
Should such deposit be made, the sentence of imprisonment shall stand set aside and the appellant discharged of his bail bond.
However, in the event of no such deposit being made, the appellant shall surrender before the trial court to serve the remainder of the prison term.
10. For a period of three months, or till the date of deposit of the increased fine amount before the MACT, whichever is earlier, the benefit of exemption from surrendering shall continue.
11. Immediately after expiry of three months from date, the MACT may intimate the Registry of this Court regarding compliance of the terms of this order.
If the appellant fails to comply, office shall seek directions.
12. The appeal stands partly allowed, on the above terms.

13. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
.............................J. [DIPANKAR DATTA] ..............................J. [AUGUSTINE GEORGE MASIH] New Delhi;
October 06, 2025.
